subject: Follow-up: buying gateway stitch & MAP draft
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@biome-tech.com>, Devon Clarke <devon.clarke@biome-tech.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: buying gateway stitch & MAP draft

Hi Asha / Devon — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed mutual action plan (attached draft) so we can align on timeline and owners.

Call highlights:
- Economic buyer: Asha indicated final sign-off is with Devon (CFO).
- Primary decision criteria: predictable per-token cost under heavy inference, SLA for 99th pct latency, and data residency for clinical test vectors.
- Security/compliance asks: SOC 2 snapshot, ID of encryption-in-transit keys, and a short runbook for audit logs.
- Procurement rhythm: procurement team needs redline window (7 business days) + PO date target.

Proposed MAP (attached: biome_map_draft_v1.xlsx) — high level milestones:
1) Technical POC kickoff (owner: Soojin) — target: 2026-08-24 — deliverable: 3-day latency/cost baseline report
2) Security evidence exchange (owner: Marissa) — target: 2026-08-28 — deliverable: SOC2 snapshot + KMS integration notes
3) Commercial review & redline (owner: Devon / procurement) — target: 2026-09-03 — deliverable: redlined SOW/contract
4) Executive sign-off / PO (owner: Devon) — target: 2026-09-10

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Asha: confirm that Devon is the final approver and whether procurement will need a separate packet (name/contact).
- Devon / procurement: are the commercial milestones above plausible for your calendar?
- Soojin: can you confirm resource availability for a POC starting 8/24 (3 days)?

Attachments: biome_map_draft_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), SOC2-snapshot-answers.pdf (answers to high-level SOC 2 questions). I can produce a short runbook for audit log access after we get the PO window.

Thanks — appreciate the time and clarity. If we can lock the MAP milestones this week, we can hit the desired procurement window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: buying gateway stitch & MAP draft

Marissa — thank you, this is helpful. A few clarifications inline and some notes: 

> Economic buyer: Asha indicated final sign-off is with Devon (CFO).
Yes, Devon will sign. He asked that we also include our legal partner (Lina Gomez) in procurement threads — Lina handles contract redlines. Her email is procurement@biome-tech.com.

> Primary decision criteria... data residency for clinical test vectors.
We need confirmation that data in the POC environment stays in us-west-2 and that logs are retained for 90 days. Can Redwood support that?

> Security/compliance asks...
The SOC2 snapshot looks good. Two asks: 1) can you provide a short mapping of controls related to encryption key management (we use HSM-backed keys), and 2) evidence of quarterly vulnerability scans (report or attestation).

PO timing: our procurement cadence is tight in mid-september; we are aiming to issue the PO by week of 9/13 if the MAP and contract review fit that window. Devon will join the commercial call next week if we schedule it.

Next steps from our side:
- I will introduce Lina (procurement) to this thread early next week.
- Devon will set aside 30 minutes for commercial review subject to calendar availability.

Thanks — Asha

Subject: Re: Follow-up: buying gateway stitch & MAP draft — POC logistics

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick technical note on the POC and data residency: 

- We can provision a POC environment in us-west-2 and restrict network egress to that region.
- For the 90-day log retention, we have a configurable retention layer and can retain request/response logs for 90 days; we will mark the POC bucket as private and provide role-based access.
- On encryption: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) and can share a controls mapping doc; attaching a brief compatibility note.

Attachment: infra_compatibility_notes.pdf (short compatibility + runbook summary).

POC staffing: I can lead the technical POC with one infra engineer (available week of 8/24). I propose the following POC plan: 
- Day 1: baseline model latency/cost test with sample clinical vectors
- Day 2: KV cache and batching configuration that mimics your production batch sizes
- Day 3: end-to-end integration test + deliver baseline report and recommended config

If procurement needs any addendum or security vetting documentation during the POC, I can prepare a one-page cert that outlines what evidence we'll provide.

Soojin Lee
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
